chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Turning down a Coca-Cola overseas tour
summary: Thomas, afraid of flying, planned to go by ship until Babe pointed out the ocean was mined, and he dropped out of the Coca-Cola overseas tour.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: May I interrupt you for a minute? Because it was during that time when he was with Teddy that the Coca-Cola people wanted the band to go overseas and so they presented the idea ...
So, they approached Joe with this overseas idea so Joe had come home and talked to me about it, said salute they value if the loot
is right, I'm going to make it. So the war is on as you know. So I said, fine. I knew Joe had no eyes for flying at all so he said ...
Way up there in the air.

And, at that time he had never flown. So I said, Well, you know Joe, you're going to have to fly if this comes through, you're going to have to fly. He said, No, no, I'm not flying. That's out. Definitely out. They'll just have to let me know in time and I'll leave before anyone else. If nobody else wants to go when I go, that's all right.

He said, I'll just take me a nice slow boat and go to Europe. So I'm thinking about this and a couple of days later I'm talking to him again about it and said, Joe, you know one thing. You can't go by boat. He said, Why can't I go by boat. I said, Because the whole ocean is mined. They're liable to blow you up. He looked at me very seriously and he said, Coca-Cola people I'm out.

What happened, Eddie Condor, we had done some things at Town Hall, at Carnegie Hall, you know ... with the Coca-Cola people. And, what the hell, I needed the money. It sounds good. We had a good group of musicians there. I think it's going to be nice and quiet. She disrupted my idea altogether. ... that was over.
